name: Law of Torts and Consumer Protection
seo_title: UGC NET Law Torts and Consumer Protection Notes (Unit 5)
description: UGC NET Law Torts & Consumer Protection notes: 12 topics, 114 sub-topics on torts, the CPA 2019, Motor Vehicles Act and Competition Act. Free, with revision mode.
intro: Unit V combines English and Indian case law in torts with three statutes: the Consumer Protection Act, the Motor Vehicles Act and the Competition Act. Topic 0 explains the exam pattern and the repealed-1986-Act trap. Topics 1 to 3 cover the nature of tort, general principles and defences; Topic 4 covers negligence, nuisance, trespass and defamation; Topics 5 to 7 cover remoteness, strict and absolute liability and State liability; Topics 8 to 10 cover the three statutes, and Topic 11 is a rapid revision sheet of case anchors, numbers and concept traps.
how: Start with Topic 0, then read Topics 1 to 10 in order. Learn each case with its principle in one line; Topic 4 is the longest, so take Negligence, Nuisance, Trespass and Defamation one at a time.
Switch on Revision mode on any topic page to keep each section's key terms, lists and tables. For the statutes (Topics 8 to 10) learn the amounts, periods and the latest amendments.
Use the rapid-recall sheet (numbers and periods, concept traps), then Topic 11 and practice MCQs.

1.seo_title: Nature and Definition of Tort Notes: Maxims, Remedies | UGC NET Law
1.description: UGC NET Law notes on the nature of tort: definitions, essential elements, foundational maxims, intention and malice, pigeon-hole theory, remedies and discharge.
1.lead: Meaning and definitions, essential elements, the maxims (damnum sine injuria, injuria sine damno), mental element, theories of liability, remedies and discharge.

2.seo_title: General Principles of Tortious Liability | UGC NET Law
2.description: UGC NET Law notes on general principles of tort: conditions, act and omission, legal damage, parties, vicarious liability and constitutional torts.
2.lead: The basic conditions, act and omission, legal damage, who can sue and be sued, vicarious liability, strict liability overview and constitutional torts.

3.seo_title: General Defences in Tort: Volenti, Necessity | UGC NET Law
3.description: UGC NET Law notes on general defences in tort: volenti non fit injuria, necessity, private defence, act of God, inevitable accident, mistake, statutory authority.
3.lead: Volenti, necessity, private defence, act of God, inevitable accident, mistake, statutory authority, contributory negligence and judicial acts.

related.why: Defences specific to negligence, nuisance and defamation
Exceptions to the rule in Rylands v Fletcher

4.seo_title: Negligence, Nuisance, Trespass, Defamation Notes | UGC NET Law
4.description: UGC NET Law notes on specific torts: negligence (duty of care, medical negligence), nuisance, trespass to person, land and goods, and defamation with defences.
4.lead: Negligence in ten parts, nuisance in six, trespass in three and defamation in seven, each with elements, defences, remedies and leading cases.

5.seo_title: Remoteness of Damages: Polemis, Wagon Mound | UGC NET Law
5.description: UGC NET Law notes on remoteness of damage: Re Polemis directness test, Wagon Mound foreseeability, thin skull rule, novus actus interveniens and causation in fact.
5.lead: The directness test, the foreseeability test, Wagon Mound (No. 2), the thin skull rule, intervening causes, causation in fact and the Indian position.

related.why: Negligence, where remoteness is mostly applied

6.seo_title: Strict and Absolute Liability: Rylands v Fletcher | UGC NET Law
6.description: UGC NET Law notes on strict and absolute liability: Rylands v Fletcher, exceptions, English cases, M.C. Mehta (Oleum Gas), Bhopal and no-fault statutes.
6.lead: The rule in Rylands v Fletcher, its ingredients and exceptions, developments in England, India's absolute liability and other no-fault statutes.

related.why: No-fault liability under the Motor Vehicles Act

7.seo_title: State Liability in Tort: Kasturi Lal, Rudul Sah | UGC NET Law
7.description: UGC NET Law notes on State liability in tort: sovereign and non-sovereign functions, Kasturi Lal, constitutional torts and public-law compensation under Article 21.
7.lead: The English rule and Article 300, the pre-constitution cases, the Supreme Court cases after 1950, constitutional torts, procedure and law reform.

8.seo_title: Consumer Protection Act 2019 Notes: CCPA | UGC NET Law
8.description: UGC NET Law notes on consumer protection: CPA 1986 definitions, rights, redressal machinery, the CPA 2019 changes (CCPA, product liability, mediation) and cases.
8.lead: The 1986 Act's definitions, rights and redressal machinery, then the 2019 Act's key changes, recent regulations and leading cases.

related.why: Motor accident claims, another statutory remedy

9.seo_title: Motor Vehicles Act 1988 Notes: No-Fault, MACT | UGC NET Law

9.lead: No-fault liability, compulsory third-party insurance, Motor Accident Claims Tribunals, how compensation is determined and the 2019 amendment.

related.why: Negligence, the basis of fault claims

10.seo_title: Competition Act 2002 Notes: Dominance, 2023 Amendment | UGC NET Law

10.lead: The Act's background and institutions, anti-competitive agreements, abuse of dominant position, combinations, penalties and the 2023 amendment.
